newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bendigo says plans underground mines.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bendigo says plans underground mines.

text.p: Bendigo Mining NL said on Wednesday it plans to apply for approval to establish two long term underground mining operations in the Bendigo Goldfields of Victoria, one at the Williams United site at Eaglehawk and the other targeting the Deborah Reef in central Bendigo.
Managing Director Doug Buerger said the intention in both cases was to develop declines to access the target ore bodies.
Bendigo Mining said it had identified 180,000 ounces of gold resources on the Deborah Line of Reef - the last to be discovered and mined on the Bendigo goldfield.
At the Williams United site, the company said it had identified an underground mining resource of 31,000 ounces of gold and an open pit reserve of 25,000 ounces.
"Both underground prospects have great potential for expansion and exploration for gold is continuing," Buerger said in a statement released to the Australian Stock Exchange.

He said the underground declines provided real hope for substantial long term mining operations on the Bendigo field. He said the resources were the result of extensive exploration by Bendigo Mining and previously by WMC Ltd.
Buerger said Bendigo Mining's existing applications for approval to undertake surface mining at Williams United, Eaglehawk and the Birds/Carshalton site, Kangaroo Flat would still proceed.
"These operations are important to plans for establishing a long term gold mining industry in Bendigo," he said.
